name: Western Blot – Day 1
description: Day 1 of Western blotting: protein sample preparation, SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis, transfer to membrane, blocking, and overnight primary antibody incubation.
source_note: General educational template for standard Western blot workflow.

steps.title: Sample preparation — cell/tissue lysis
steps.description: Lyse cells or tissue in RIPA or equivalent lysis buffer containing protease inhibitors (and phosphatase inhibitors if needed). Incubate on ice with occasional vortexing, then centrifuge to clear the lysate.
steps.notes: Collect supernatant (cleared lysate) carefully avoiding fat layer and pellet.
steps.warnings: Add lysis buffer ice-cold. Protease inhibitors degrade quickly — prepare fresh.

steps.title: Protein quantification (BCA or Bradford assay)
steps.description: Determine protein concentration of each sample using BCA assay (Bradford or Lowry are alternatives). Use BSA standards. Goal: load equal amounts of protein per well (typically 20–50 µg).

reagents.name: BCA Reagent A + B (2:50 working solution)

steps.notes: Run samples in duplicate. Read absorbance at 562 nm.

steps.title: Prepare sample loading buffer and denature
steps.description: Normalize sample volumes based on protein quantification. Add 4× or 6× Laemmli loading buffer (containing SDS + β-mercaptoethanol or DTT). Heat at 95–100°C to denature proteins.

reagents.name: 4× Laemmli SDS sample buffer (with DTT or β-ME)
Sample dilution buffer (lysis buffer or water)

equipment: Heat block at 95°C or boiling water bath
steps.notes: Let samples cool briefly. Centrifuge to pellet any insoluble material.
steps.warnings: β-mercaptoethanol is toxic and volatile. Handle in fume hood.

steps.title: Prepare and run SDS-PAGE gel
steps.description: Assemble gel in electrophoresis tank. Fill with 1× running buffer. Load pre-stained molecular weight ladder and denatured protein samples. Run at 80–100 V through stacking gel, then 120–150 V through resolving gel.
steps.notes: Use 10% gel for proteins 30–100 kDa; 12–15% for <30 kDa; 4–8% for >100 kDa. Run until dye front reaches the bottom.
steps.warnings: Electric shock hazard. Ensure lid is properly closed before turning on power.

steps.title: Activate membrane
steps.description: Prepare PVDF or nitrocellulose membrane. PVDF: pre-wet in 100% methanol for 30 sec, then equilibrate in transfer buffer. Nitrocellulose: equilibrate directly in transfer buffer. Pre-wet blotting papers and sponges/pads.

reagents.name: PVDF or nitrocellulose membrane (cut to gel size)

equipment: Transfer tank or semi-dry transfer system
steps.notes: Do not let PVDF dry out after activation. Keep membrane wet in transfer buffer.
steps.warnings: Methanol is flammable and toxic. Work in ventilated area.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to membrane
steps.description: Assemble the transfer sandwich (sponge/paper/gel/membrane/paper/sponge). Run wet transfer at 80–100 V for 1–2 h (on ice + stir bar), or semi-dry at 20 V / 1 mA per cm² for 30–45 min.
steps.shakingRotation: Add stir bar to tank during transfer
steps.notes: Check orientation: membrane faces positive electrode (red). A pre-stained ladder that transfers confirms successful transfer. High MW proteins may need overnight 4°C transfer.
steps.warnings: High voltage — ensure lid is closed. Keep tank cold to prevent gel from melting.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.description: Block non-specific antibody binding sites on the membrane. Standard blocking: 5% non-fat dried milk in TBST (or PBST). For phospho-proteins, use 5% BSA in TBST. Incubate on a rocker.

reagents.name: 5% non-fat milk or 5% BSA in TBST

steps.notes: Use BSA (not milk) for phospho-protein or HRP-conjugated antibodies. Milk contains casein (a phosphoprotein) that can interfere.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation (overnight at 4°C)
steps.description: Prepare primary antibody at recommended dilution in 5% milk or BSA/TBST. Briefly wash membrane with TBST, then incubate in primary antibody overnight at 4°C on a rocker.
steps.notes: Incubation can also be done at RT for 2 h if 4°C is not feasible. Antibody solution can be reused 2–4 times if stored at 4°C + azide.
